Foreign particles were detected inside one HDPE drum of Metformin API batch MFH260712A during incoming inspection; the drum was quarantined and the particles were metallic or carbonaceous in nature, with no external damage observed.

672422ab-7614-41e0-b942-81f179cb2f2b.risk_justification: Risk assessment could not be completed by the AI. Defaulted to Major/High — please review manually.
672422ab-7614-41e0-b942-81f179cb2f2b.root_cause_hypothesis: The most probable cause is ingress of metallic/carbonaceous particles during bulk transfer from the reactor to the HDPE drum due to inadequate cleaning and wear of the stainless‑steel transfer line/valve assembly. A worn gasket or corroded valve seat generated metal shavings, while carbonaceous residues originated from degraded polymeric seals. The cleaning validation for the bulk‑handling equipment was insufficient, allowing residual particles to contaminate the API during drum filling, consistent with 21 CFR 211.67 (equipment cleaning) and ICH Q10 (continuous improvement).
672422ab-7614-41e0-b942-81f179cb2f2b.capa_text:
Corrective Actions:
1. Quarantine the entire MFH260712A batch and perform a full visual and metal‑detector inspection of all drums.
2. Segregate and disposition the contaminated drum (re‑process if feasible, otherwise destroy per SOP).
3. Conduct an immediate on‑site inspection of the bulk transfer line, valve assembly, and associated fittings; replace any worn or corroded components.
4. Perform a thorough cleaning of the transfer equipment using validated procedures; re‑run a cleaning verification (swab and rinse analysis) before resuming production.
5. Document the investigation, findings, and corrective steps in a CAPA record (21 CFR 820.100).

Preventive Actions:
1. Revise the Cleaning Validation SOP for bulk‑handling equipment to include wear‑monitoring criteria (e.g., visual inspection, torque checks, and periodic metallographic sampling) and to require a post‑cleaning metal‑detector check.
2. Implement a preventive‑maintenance program for all stainless‑steel transfer lines and pneumatic valves, with defined intervals for gasket replacement and surface‑roughness verification (per USP <61>/<62>).
3. Install an in‑line metal‑detector or particle‑counter on the transfer line to provide real‑time detection of foreign particles before drum filling.
4. Update the Drum Filling SOP to require a pre‑fill drum integrity check (visual, ultrasonic) and a documented drum‑cleanliness verification.
5. Provide targeted training for operators and cleaning personnel on contamination control, equipment wear signs, and proper documentation of cleaning activities.
6. Conduct a supplier audit of drum manufacturers to verify that drums are supplied clean, unused, and free of internal contaminants; require a Certificate of Conformance for each lot.
7. Integrate the above changes into the QMS as part of the ICH Q10 quality‑system model, ensuring periodic review of effectiveness through internal audits and trend analysis of foreign‑particle complaints.
8. Establish a KPI for foreign‑particle incidents (target = 0 per quarter) and review it in the monthly quality‑review meeting.
All actions shall be tracked, verified for effectiveness, and closed per CAPA closure criteria before releasing any remaining product from batch MFH260712A.

32e10849-01e3-4d30-8a41-cebacca5deb1.risk_justification: Risk assessment could not be completed by the AI. Defaulted to Major/High — please review manually.
32e10849-01e3-4d30-8a41-cebacca5deb1.root_cause_hypothesis: The foreign particles most likely originated from equipment wear during the milling step. A stainless‑steel grinding mill (or its agitator shaft/ grinding media) showed excessive wear, releasing metallic and carbonaceous fragments that entered the bulk Metformin API stream. Inadequate preventive‑maintenance inspection of wear parts and the absence of an in‑process metal‑detector checkpoint allowed these particles to be transferred into the HDPE drums during filling, resulting in contamination of the 25 kg lot.
32e10849-01e3-4d30-8a41-cebacca5deb1.capa_text:
Corrective Actions:
1. Quarantine the affected drum and perform a full visual and metal‑detector inspection of the remaining product in the batch.
2. Conduct a detailed investigation of the milling equipment (wear‑part inspection, dimensional check, surface analysis) and replace any degraded components.
3. Re‑process or discard the contaminated material according to 21 CFR 211.122 and ICH Q7.
4. Perform a root‑cause verification test (e.g., particle count, metal detection) on a representative sample before release.

Preventive Actions:
1. Revise the preventive‑maintenance program for the grinding mill to include wear‑part inspection frequency and acceptance criteria (per GMP Annex 15, ICH Q10).
2. Implement an in‑process metal‑detector or X‑ray inspection step after milling and before drum filling, with defined acceptance limits (per USP <2310>).
3. Update SOPs for drum filling and handling to require a pre‑use visual inspection of drums and lids, and to use protective liners inside drums.
4. Strengthen cleaning validation for transfer lines and equipment to ensure no cross‑contamination (per FDA 21 CFR 211.67).
5. Provide targeted training for operators and maintenance personnel on equipment wear monitoring, metal‑detector operation, and drum handling.
6. Document the change control in the quality‑system (ICH Q10) and perform periodic audits to verify compliance.
